description:
## Question

The repo `CLAUDE.md` now says a turnkey-owned buck2 prelude is on the table ("The Buck2 prelude is ours to change"). What form should that ownership take?

- **(a) Upstream as the source of truth.** Keep fetching the upstream prelude and carry turnkey's changes as `nix/patches/prelude/*.patch` plus `nix/buck2/prelude-extensions/`. This fits the "Importing External Software" rule in `CLAUDE.md` and is what `nix/buck2/prelude.nix` already does, though no patches exist yet.
- **(b) A real fork,** e.g. a `firefly-engineering/buck2-prelude` repo fetched by Nix and rebased on upstream periodically. It's still not a copy inside this repo, but upstream stops being the source of truth.

## Context

- Turnkey already extends the prelude with languages upstream lacks (TypeScript, Solidity, Jsonnet, mdbook) by copying extension files over the upstream tree. Extensions can also overwrite upstream files.
- The test result caching effort (turnkey-w55) will need upstream rule changes. Example: go_test/python_test only use project-relative paths under remote execution, which blocks cross-checkout reuse (see turnkey-w55.3). Per-language changes are decided in turnkey-w55.8. That effort starts with (a); this question doesn't block it.
- Upgrade cost matters for either option. The turnkey prelude currently matches buck2 release 2026-03-15 while the binary is 2026-04-15, and upgrading past the pin removes `network_access` from `ExternalRunnerTestInfo` (turnkey-w55.1).

Decide: which form, when (if ever) to move from (a) to (b), and how prelude upgrades are kept in step with the buck2 binary.
title: Should turnkey's buck2 prelude be a patch set on upstream or a real fork?
